unattended_fire.what_happened: The two-board scheme (a second daily invocation at 10:25 so the queue's next arm reaches the other board) failed on its first day. The machine was asleep at 10:05 and 10:25 local, so BOTH routes were dispatched in the same catch-up burst at 14:08:04 local, both read the submission list before either write landed, and both selected the same queue head (the AGI-2 arm). The platform refused the second CreateCodeSubmission with a 400, the readback found the row anyway and logged 'submitted', and the invocation was consumed: AGI-2's slot was spent, AGI-3's was left unfired and would have been lost for the UTC day.
unattended_fire.root_cause: Selection was deduplicated only by 'is this arm's message already on the board' -- which is a read-then-write across processes, so two invocations that start together both see the head as unfired. The 20 minutes between the routes is what was supposed to separate them, and a catch-up burst is exactly the case where it does not exist.
unattended_fire.fix: Two guards in scripts/fire_next_arm.py, both needed: (1) an OS-level exclusive lock (msvcrt on Windows, fcntl elsewhere, released by the kernel if the holder dies, so no stale-lock timeout) held across read-decide-fire, so the second invocation reads a board that already contains the first one's submission; (2) board_state() now also returns the boards that already have a submission DATED today (UTC), and select() skips their arms outright -- so however many routes fire, each board spends exactly its one slot and the queue advances to the other board instead of re-selecting a spent one.
unattended_fire.verified: self-test: selection, log-vs-board dedup, the spend guard, and a real second PROCESS holding the lock (a same-process check would pass even if locking did nothing) -- all pass. End to end: two invocations started in the same instant now both report queue_empty with spent_today = both boards (the old code selected the AGI-2 head twice); and an invocation started under a lock holder waited 18.1 s and then proceeded, i.e. it serialized instead of racing.
unattended_fire.cost: none today beyond the 400 that was already refused: no duplicate row exists on either board (AGI-2's newest row is 56597262, one row). The AGI-3 slot was recovered by hand in this session.
